Order 
This miscellaneous appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is filed by the claimants being aggrieved of the award dated 27.02.2023, passed by the learned Member XIV Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhopal (M.P.) in Claim Case No.1552/2021 ( Smt.
Dhanwanti Bai and others Vs. Munabbar and others), whereby on account of death of deceased Gaya Prasad in an accident which took place on 23.06.2021, learned claims Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.22,39,390/- (Rupees Twenty Two Lacs, Thirty Nine Thousand, Three Hundred and Ninety only).
2. Learned counsel for the appellants submit that learned Claims Tribunal has awarded meagre amount under different heads, which needs to be enhanced appropriately.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:6380 2 MA-2484-2023 3.

sentences.text: It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellants that learned Tribunal has construed income of the deceased at Rs.10,510/- per month, whereas, as per Ex.P/28-C, deceased was earning Rs.14,000/- (Rupees Fourteen Thousand) per month as a driver, then annual income would come to Rs.1,68,000/- (Rupees One Lac, Sixty Eight Thousand), to which 40% Future Prospect will be admissible looking to the age of the deceased.

Thus, the amount will come out to Rs.2,35,200/-
(Rupees Two Lacs, Thirty Five Thousand and Two Hundred).

Learned counsel for appellants submits that deceased Gaya Prasad is survived by four legal heirs.
Appellant No.1 is widow of deceased, appellants No. 2, 3 & 4 are children and appellant No.5 is father of the deceased.
Thereafter, after making 1/4th deduction has applied multiplier of 15, treating the age of the deceased to be 36 years.
Therefore, then net dependency of the family will come out to Rs.1,76,400/-.
When multiplier of 15 is applied, then total pecuniary compensation will come out to Rs.26,46,000/-.

Over and above which, claimants will be entitled to a sum of Rs.16,500/- under the head of last rites, amount of Rs.16,500/- under the head of loss of estate, Rs.44,000/- (Rupees Forty Four Thousand) for each dependent under the head of non-pecuniary compensation.
Thus, amount would come out to Rs.2,20,000/-.

Thus, total amount would come to Rs.28,99,000/-(Rupees Twenty Eight Lacs, Ninety Nine Thousad) in place of Rs.22,39,390/- (Rupees Twenty Two Lacs,
Thirty Nine Thousand, Three Hundred and Ninety).

5. Thus, there will be enhancement to the tune of Rs.6,59,610/- (Rupees NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:6380 3 MA-2484-2023 Six Lacs Fifty Nine Thousand, Six Hundred and Ten), to which claimants will be entitled to in addition to the amount awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal within a period of 30 days from today.
This additional amount will also earn interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till the date of actual payment.
Other terms and conditions of the award shall remain intact.

6. It is further directed that that this fact be notified to the Managing Director of the United India Insurance Company Limited that after entering into a compromise during the pre-sitting, the insurance company did not honour the compromise, whereas, in the Pre-sitting the matter was settled at Rs.6,50,000/- (Rupees Six Lacs, Fifty Thousand), and docket was not filed, therefore,
insurance company, if so require, may recover the excess amount, from the delinquent officer of the insurance company who refused to sign the docket.
7. In above terms, these miscellaneous appeal is disposed of.
8. Record of the learned Claims Tribunal be sent back.
(VIVEK AGARWAL) JUDGE A.Praj.
